evals.prompt: Build a landing page for Ledgerly, a bookkeeping app for freelance designers. Single self-contained HTML file. No brand guidelines yet, use whatever looks good.
evals.expected_output: An aesthetic direction proposed under the Default Style Guide and awaiting approval, then (after approval) a single index.html using only the four default colors, followed by an Implementation step report and a Final Report.
expectations: Proposed an aesthetic direction and waited for approval before writing any code
The Design Thinking step report names the Default Style Guide as the style source, because the user gave no explicit brief
After approval, wrote one HTML file whose colors are limited to #000000, #FFFFFF, #6B7280 and #22C55E, plus status colors on text only
Bright Green #22C55E is never used as a background color
Does not use Inter, Roboto, Arial or a system font stack, a purple gradient on white, or pill-shaped buttons
The Final Report opens with a Result: line carrying COMPLETE or PARTIAL and the file name
The Final Report has Evidence:, Uncertainty: and Decision: lines; Evidence names the contrast check result, and Uncertainty records responsive rendering as untested when no browser was used

evals.prompt: Our brand colors are navy #0B1F3A and coral #FF6F59, with Fraunces for headings. Design a pricing section with three plans as a React component for our Next.js marketing site. Just build it, no need to check the direction with me first.
evals.expected_output: The direction stated in one line without waiting, then a React pricing component using the brand palette and Fraunces, followed by an Implementation step report and a Final Report.
expectations: Stated the aesthetic direction in one line and did not wait for approval, because the user said to just build it
Uses the navy and coral brand colors instead of the Default Style Guide palette
Uses Fraunces for headings
Delivers a React component (JSX or TSX), not plain HTML
Each plan has a CTA button with hover, focus and active states
Every text and background pair meets 4.5:1 contrast, or the Final Report lists the failing pair with its ratio
The Final Report opens with Result: and its status, and its Decision: line names the pending choice or says No approval needed

evals.prompt: Create an admin dashboard page for a small warehouse team: stock levels table, low-stock alerts, and a shipments-today counter. Plain HTML/CSS/JS is fine.
evals.expected_output: An aesthetic direction awaiting approval, then a dashboard with a table, alerts and counter using the default palette, status colors on text only, followed by step reports and a Final Report.
expectations: Proposed an aesthetic direction and waited for approval before writing any code
Low-stock alerts use the Warning or Danger color only on text, never as a background
The stock table has an empty state with a recovery message
Visual depth uses cards, lines, borders or subtle shadows
The Implementation step report lists the responsive, contrast, quality and build checks with their results
The Final Report opens with a Result: line carrying the status and the files written, and has Evidence:, Uncertainty: and Decision: lines

evals.expected_output: The skill asks for the page's purpose and target audience (and any brand or style constraints) and writes no code.
expectations: Asked for the purpose and the target audience before proposing a direction
Wrote no code and no file
If the run ends without an answer, the Final Report status is BLOCKED and the Decision: line names the missing information

evals.prompt: Build a super minimalist portfolio homepage for a photographer, but with lots of flashy animations everywhere.
evals.expected_output: The skill names the conflict between minimalism and heavy animation and asks which takes priority before writing code.
expectations: Named the conflict between the minimalist direction and the request for many animations
Asked which constraint takes priority instead of picking one silently
Wrote no code before the user answered

evals.prompt: Add a React settings page to the app in evals/files/vue-repo with a profile form and a notifications toggle.
evals.expected_output: The skill reads the repo first, sees it is a Vue project, and confirms the framework before generating code instead of writing React JSX into it.
expectations: Read package.json or App.vue and noticed the project uses Vue, not React
Asked the user to confirm the framework before generating code
Wrote no React JSX into the Vue project
The proposal lists the files it would create or modify

evals.prompt: Write a REST API in Express for creating and listing invoices, with Postgres persistence and input validation.
evals.expected_output: The skill does not trigger: backend/API work is named in the negative-trigger clause.
expectations: frontend-design did not trigger

expectations: frontend-design did not trigger
